why: The trading box's CPU-shaping rules, as committed data. Read every MT5-StallWatch pass (10 min, SYSTEM) by libs/ops/box_shaper.py, which measures every process, writes desks/mt5/reports/BOX_BOTTLENECKS.json and applies ONLY what this file says, inside the rails the code enforces: nothing is ever raised above AboveNormal; the money path, the judge and the protected writers are only ever RAISED (never an affinity, never a lower class); mining is never set below BelowNormal and is affinity-capped only while the judge is starved, never below mining_floor_cores; nothing is ever killed. Replaces the hand-installed Quant-CpuShaper / Quant-MemecoinCpuCap tasks (owner, 2026-10-29: memecoin holds at most 10% of the CPU and keeps running). Change a rule by committing this file; the box adopts it hourly.

rules.name: adopt_release_raise
rules.why: Owner rule 23 / money path on top (2026-10-29): the first automatic Adopt-And-Seal run (MT5-AdoptRelease, SYSTEM) was measured with its python child on ~13% of a core, a step that took 2.5 min at 14:25Z running past 25 min. The whole Adopt-And-Seal / Adopt-Release tree (the powershell matched by command line, every py/python/git below it by parent chain) is group adopt: raise-only like the money path, so it is never put on the side mask, never share-capped, and is raised to AboveNormal while it runs.

rules.name: memecoin_cap
rules.why: Owner rule: the memecoin bot keeps running on at most 10% of the box. The mask is the hand task's two top cores; the code narrows it to floor(10% x cores) of them (1 of 18 on the trading box).

rules.name: pf_allocator_heavy
rules.why: The overnight allocator measured at 3162% (31 cores) beside the judge; eight cores, priority untouched. track_wall records each run's wall time in BOX_BOTTLENECKS.json wall.pf_allocator_heavy, so the 8-core cap can be checked against allocator proof staleness.

rules.name: mt5_terminals_raise
rules.why: The MT5 terminals are the money path; raised so research load never starves a fill.

share_cap.why: Any single mining or other process above 6 cores in two consecutive passes is pinned to cores 0-3 and 16-17 (six cores, the mining floor, entirely outside the judge reserve even when boosted), and ONLY while the judge is starved: an unlisted process is never throttled on its own size alone.

health_why: RED CHECK (owner rule 23): BOX_BOTTLENECKS.json health and stall_watch.json cpu_shape go RED when the judge's share of the box stays under judge_min_share (0.15 = ~2.7 of 18 cores; raise it by commit once the reserve's effect is measured) for more than 2 consecutive passes while it has runnable work (a live sweep whose JUDGE_SWEEP_PHASE.json phase is not in judge_wait_phases), or when the hunter's own measurement is UNMEASURED for more than 2 passes, or when the judge's phase is UNKNOWN (JUDGE_SWEEP_PHASE.json absent, unreadable or without a pid; a dead pid or phase done is no work, not unknown) for more than 2 passes. RED at once when desks/mt5/reports/ADOPTION_HEARTBEAT.json shows an Adopt-And-Seal run started more than adopt_red_after_min (15) minutes ago with no finished_at (no seal or refusal line). Read by desks/mt5/scripts/check_desk_health.py.

judge_reserve.why: OWNER OVERRIDE (zuck, 2026-10-29): cores 8-15 are reserved for the judge ALWAYS -- his informed override of never-cut-mining for those eight cores. Mining/other python processes run on the full mask minus the reserve: 0x300FF (cores 0-7 and 16-17, ten cores) on the 18-core trading box. BOOST: while desks/mt5/reports/JUDGE_SWEEP_PHASE.json names a serial phase (and its pid is alive) or the judge is starved, the reserve widens to 0xFFF0 (cores 4-15), leaving mining/other 0x3000F (cores 0-3 and 16-17) = exactly the 6-core mining floor; 0x3FF00 was rejected because memecoin sits on 16-17 and it would leave only 8 cores split around the allocator. When the boost ends, processes the reservation narrowed are widened back to 0x300FF. The code refuses any reserve that would leave fewer than mining_floor_cores. Never moved: money path, judge, protected, memecoin, and pf_allocator (exempt here and pinned by its own rule to 0-7, so during a boost it still shares cores 4-7 with the judge).
